## Context
The original failure recorded on innovative-dandruffy-deer remained a distinct unresolved symptom: in Gerrit Verified run 31775418405, the authorship fixture merge reported an invalid object for a freshly committed loose blob and git write-tree failed. Direct deletion reproduced the byte-for-byte signature, but the organic deleter was not identified. Gerrit 1769 added object-store forensics for the next occurrence.

The later Gerrit 1827 failure did not reproduce this class: deleting the implicated blob left both broad and narrow history reads healthy. That later batched-empty / narrow-success recurrence was a separate fixture-contract defect fixed by merged Gerrit 1828. This ticket preserved the unresolved ENOENT work until the organic recurrence in Change 1855 exposed the detached-maintenance mechanism.

## Plan
- On the next organic recurrence, collect the Gerrit 1769 forensic block (fsck, count-objects, object listing with mtimes, and GIT_* environment).
- Identify and deterministically reproduce the process or environment mechanism that removes or hides a freshly committed reachable loose object.
- Add a RED regression for the proven mechanism, fix the mechanism class without weakening the fixture topology, and prove GREEN plus exact-defect mutation coverage.
- Run the repository gates and land through Gerrit before closing.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] An organic recurrence supplies the captured object-store forensic block, or an equivalent deterministic local reproduction identifies the deleter.
- [x] The deleting or object-hiding mechanism is proven rather than inferred from the invalid-object signature alone.
- [x] A behavioral regression is observed RED before the class fix and GREEN afterward.
- [x] The exact-defect mutation returns the regression to RED.
- [x] Repository lint, typecheck, full tests, Gerrit LLM-Review, and Verified gates pass.
